concept: macOS 27 IOGPUFamily changes and whether the panic is fixed
summary: Apple's macOS 27 release notes list no IOGPUFamily, kernel-panic, GPU-watchdog or Metal-hang entry. Their Metal section holds only two sampler clamp-to-edge fixes.

facts.text: Apple's macOS 27 release notes list no IOGPUFamily, kernel-panic, GPU-watchdog or Metal-hang entry. Their Metal section holds only two sampler clamp-to-edge fixes.
The only macOS 27 evidence on the panic is a mitigation that still works on IOGPUFamily 162.11. With wiring on, nobody has reported a result, because testing risks a reboot.

A different macOS 27 failure is documented in oMLX 3706: `mx.synchronize()` in the periodic cache-clear drain fails with `kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorTimeout`, and after one to three of these the driver rejects all later submissions (`SubmissionsIgnored`, a "penalty box"). It needs a second process actively submitting Metal work.
oMLX 4224's Hang class does not need macOS 27: two of its ten events ran on 26.5.1.
2026-09-14: macOS 27.0 "Golden Gate" ships as build 26A428 (SDK 26A425 in Xcode 27 27A266a).
2026-09-15 17:56: the oMLX 3706 host upgrades from 26.5.1; the first Timeout arrives 2 h 23 m after the first macOS 27 boot, after zero in 156 engine starts since 2026-06-20.
2026-09-16: oMLX commit 5941f68 makes `SubmissionsIgnored` terminate the process so a supervisor restarts it.
2026-09-21: macOS 27.2 beta 2 (26B5091g). 2026-09-28: macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), published with no developer release notes, update text "bug fixes for your Mac".
2026-10-03: oMLX 4224 opens with Hang events on 27.0 and 26.5.1.

oMLX 3706 exposure table (reporter's own probe series, M3 Ultra 512 GB, oMLX 0.5.7, mlx 0.32.0): macOS 26 with co-host serving, 130 completions, 0 faults; macOS 27 with co-host serving, 41 completions, 106 faults; macOS 27 with co-host resident but idle, 1.5 h, 0 faults; macOS 27 solo, 18.6 h, 0 faults.

The first Timeout was absorbed twice before the third tipped the process into SubmissionsIgnored; after a restart a single Timeout tipped it at once, so the driver's error budget is not simply per process lifetime.

A held process in the penalty box keeps about 400 GB wired and still answers `/v1/models` in 3 ms while generating nothing, so only an external generation probe or exit-on-SubmissionsIgnored detects it.
The reporter first blamed a scheduling-priority gap (co-host at `Nice=-5`, `ProcessType=Interactive`), measured it on 09-20, and withdrew it: priority parity changed nothing.
The maintainer could not reproduce the original Timeout on a newer oMLX and MLX and shipped only the exit patch, so the Timeout root cause is open.
A separate open oMLX thread, issue 1835, is titled "macOS 27: long-context inference 10x slower than macOS 26.6 (even after HOST_VM_INFO64 fix)"; its body was not read.

Is macOS 27 required for the concurrent-submission failures? The 3706 reporter says "necessary but not sufficient" for the Timeout class; the 4224 reporter says not required for the Hang class (2 of 10 events on 26.5.1). Different error classes, different hosts, not reconciled.
Is the prepare-count panic fixed on 27? No source says yes; MetalGuard's 0.9.0 notes say 26.4.x and a 26.5 beta had not fixed it (2026-04-25). Silence on 27 is not evidence of a fix.
Does IOGPUFamily 162.x still underflow the prepare count with MLX wiring on? Untested by anyone found.
What changed on macOS 27 so that a second Metal process trips Timeout in the drain? Maintainer could not reproduce on newer builds; Apple silent.
Does 27.0.1 (26A434) or 27.2 change any of this? No report found.
macOS 27.0 shipped on 2026-09-14 as build 26A428 with SDK build 26A425 inside Xcode 27 (27A266a).
macOS 27.2 beta 2 is build 26B5091g dated 2026-09-21, and macOS 27.0.1 is build 26A434 dated 2026-09-28 with no developer release notes.
Apple's update text for macOS 27.0.1 is "This update provides bug fixes for your Mac."
Apple's macOS 27 release notes contain no entry naming IOGPUFamily, a kernel panic, a GPU watchdog or a Metal hang; the Metal section holds only two sampler clamp-to-edge fixes.
Apple's notes refer to an "Apple 10 GPU family" and say arm64e.x1 devices include Mac computers with M6 or later chips.

oMLX issue 3706 (opened 2026-09-16, M3 Ultra 512 GB, oMLX 0.5.7, mlx 0.32.0, mlx-lm 0.31.3, `iogpu.wired_limit_mb` 507904) reports `kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorTimeout` from `mx.synchronize()` in `_sync_and_clear_cache` on macOS 27.0.
The 3706 host saw zero Timeout or SubmissionsIgnored errors across 156 engine starts from 2026-06-20 on macOS 26.5.1, and the first Timeout 2 h 23 m after its first macOS 27 boot.
The 3706 host recorded 106 faults after the upgrade; every fault hour but two had a banked probe row showing a second Metal-heavy process actively serving.
On the 3706 host, macOS 26 with the second process serving gave 130 completions and 0 faults; macOS 27 with it serving gave 41 completions and 106 faults.
On the 3706 host, macOS 27 with the second process resident but idle gave 1.5 h and 0 faults, and macOS 27 solo gave 18.6 h and 0 faults.
The 3706 reporter concludes macOS 27 is "necessary but not sufficient" and that the second required ingredient is concurrent submission, not co-residence.
The 3706 reporter withdrew a scheduling-priority theory after removing `Nice=-5` and `Interactive` from the co-host changed nothing.
On the 3706 host a Timeout was absorbed twice and the third tipped the process into `SubmissionsIgnored` in the same second; after a restart a single Timeout tipped it at once.
A 3706 engine took its first Timeout about 2.5 minutes after model load, inside its own startup decode smoke test, printed ready anyway, and could not generate 11 minutes later.
The oMLX maintainer could not reproduce the original Timeout on a newer build and committed `5941f68` so that `SubmissionsIgnored` terminates the process.
The 3706 reporter says a plain second `omlx serve` under sustained load beside a large resident model should reproduce the fault.
oMLX issue 3706 links an open thread, issue 1835, titled "macOS 27: long-context inference 10x slower than macOS 26.6 (even after HOST_VM_INFO64 fix)".
Of oMLX 4224's ten Hang events, eight ran on macOS 27.0 (26A428) and two on macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), so the Hang class does not need macOS 27.
On macOS 27.0 GA (oMLX 4224 host, `iogpu.wired_limit_mb` 506880) 503.6 GB wired with 0.22 GB free ran without a hang or a prepare-count panic, using mlx 0.32.2.
MetalGuard 0.9.0 (2026-04-25) states that macOS 26.4.x and a 26.5 beta had not fixed the prepare-count panic.
No source found reports a prepare-count panic on any macOS 27 build or reports a fixed IOGPUFamily version.
